objective: 0.3.0 pi 4/10: Implement the Pi extension entry that sets the session role, adds Intent status to the context and keeps non-root sessions informed, so HolyAgent state is visible in every Pi session it applies to.
requirements: Maintainer (verbatim): "please add intents for the next 0.3.0 release where I will implement the pi extension integration"; the maintainer implements 0.3.0, so these Intents record the work and carry no Assignments until the maintainer starts it.
Maintainer (verbatim): "in the docs/pi/ it's supposed to use already existent extensions for required functionality" and "the first provider to implement will be kimi for coding global".

Release model: work lands on release/0.3.0/integration cut from main, as one release/0.3.0/<type>/<change> branch and one PR per change; the first PR of the release carries the version bump made with mise run bump:minor.
Done means mise run verify passes with the generated output in sync (mise run build) and CI green on every required check, including the windows job.

The extension is a default-exported factory receiving ExtensionAPI; it starts no process, socket, watcher or timer in the factory, and does that in session_start and releases it in an idempotent session_shutdown.
A launch flag (pi.registerFlag, pi.getFlag) selects the role: root, specialist child, or any other session. Open: flag name and values.

On session start (startup, reload, new, resume, fork) and after compaction (session_compact) the extension runs holyagent status through pi.exec, and holyagent reconcile after resume and compaction, and adds the result as a message on the next run via before_agent_start or pi.sendMessage, never by changing the system prompt.
The status context stays within the 9,300-character budget of the Claude hook and adds nothing when the project has no .holyagent folder.
In a non-root session the extension adds the marked core span of the root rules; the root process gets the full text in its system prompt and only the status.
Handlers are short and fail closed; the extension works in TUI, RPC, JSON and print modes.
The extension reaches the runtime through the scripts/holyagent wrapper shipped in the package, unchanged.
Open: how the root process is started (the research says a launch with --append-system-prompt and -e; it names no launcher).
Open: whether the extension loads with -e (the research's recommendation), by a global pi install (the Claude-parity assumption), or both.
Maintainer (verbatim): "the pi extension and integration will use a config.json that will set options, functionality, the provider, which will enable/disable its deps, etc".

The Pi extension reads one config.json that sets the integration's options, which functionality is on, and the model provider; enabling or disabling a function or provider in it enables or disables the existing pi extensions and packages that supply it, so a disabled one is neither loaded nor required.
config.json is decoded with Effect Schema (onExcessProperty: "error") at load, with documented defaults; an invalid file stops with a message naming the field instead of falling back silently.

Open: where config.json lives (project, user or both, and which wins), whether it is the existing .holyagent/config.json extended or a separate file, its full option list, and how a change takes effect (restart or reload).
Maintainer (verbatim): "there will be no auto-mode, full access shall be the default".
Pi sessions and the specialists the root launches run with full access by default: no auto-mode gate or approval reviewer is loaded, and project trust is granted (children pass --approve).
